parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘improving learning effectiveness’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the PQRST study skill. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have found out about perspectives on learning.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
We have theory and we have the real world. Evaluate what psychologists have found out
about different perspectives on learning and include a discussion of applications to education.

Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe one specific technique to help children overcome their dyslexia.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Children may receive specific help for their dyslexia, but they also need to be educated
generally. Suggest an appropriate strategy for educating children with special needs.

text: There is a student in your class who has dyslexia. You know this because she spells the word
discussion in three different ways: diskutian, discussian and disckussion. When you ask her about
it, she reads and says each one in exactly the same way.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe one theory which explains why we attribute causes to behaviour.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest how negative attributions, such as learned helplessness, can be changed. 
Psychology and Health
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Imagine you teach psychology and your students have to calculate statistical tests. One student
just looks at the numbers without trying and says “I can’t do maths”. He appears to have what is
called ‘learned helplessness’.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘psychogenic pain’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the gate control theory of pain proposed by Melzack. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have learned about adherence to medical advice.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
“We can count the number of pills in the bottle, but all it tells us is how many are left.” Evaluate
what psychologists have learned about adherence to medical advice, discussing the use of
quantitative and qualitative data. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe one study which has measured stress physiologically.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Physiological measures determine the level of stress. Suggest a measure to find out the
cause of stress.

text: One of your friends is stressed and you decide to measure both the level and cause of his stress.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest a strategy to help reduce accidents in the school science laboratory.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Outline the theory on which your suggestion is based. 
Psychology and Environment
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Students studying science in a school laboratory are having too many accidents. You want to find
a way to reduce the number of accidents.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘community environmental design’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one investigation into the design of either a gambling casino or a shopping mall
environment. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have learned about environmental cognition.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Laboratory experiments have control, but they may lack ecological validity. Evaluate what
psychologists have learned about environmental cognition, debating the ecological validity of
ways in which environmental cognition has been studied. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe one laboratory study which has investigated the effects of noise on pro-social
behaviour.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest what variables should be controlled, and why, in any investigation into the effects of
noise on pro-social behaviour.

text: Noise affects many different behaviours such as helping, performance and health. You decide to
conduct a laboratory investigation into the effects of noise on helping (pro-social) behaviour.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe how psychologists can prevent crowding by using visual escapes.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest how you could investigate the effectiveness of a visual escape, such as a book, on
crowded public transport. 
Psychology and Abnormality
Section A
Answer this question.

text: A train company has asked you for help in reducing the effects of crowding on busy trains. You
suggest that people should read a book, but the train company wants evidence that this will work.
You need to provide them with evidence.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by the term ‘addiction’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one way in which addiction has been defined (e.g. Griffiths, 1995). 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have found out about abnormal affect.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
“We should reduce complex behaviours to simple components to study them more easily.”
Evaluate what psychologists have found out about abnormal affect including a discussion
about the reductionist nature of explanations. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the approach on which the token economy programme is based.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would use a token economy programme for the schizophrenic patients in
your care.

text: You have just got a job working in a home for people who have schizophrenia. They all take their
medication but you want to get them to change their behaviour so they interact more with staff and
other patients. You decide to devise a token economy programme.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe one way in which obsessive compulsive disorder has been measured using a
questionnaire.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest an alternative way in which obsessive compulsive disorder can be measured without
using a questionnaire. 
Psychology and Organisations
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Psychologists often devise questionnaires to assess mental problems.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘need theory of motivation’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe McClelland’s need theory of motivation. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have found out about satisfaction at work.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
“Questionnaires are like doors. They are either open or closed.” Evaluate what psychologists
have found out about satisfaction at work and include a discussion of the use of
questionnaires to measure job satisfaction. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest an experiment to discover whether noise affects the workers’ concentration.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe evidence showing two effects of physical working conditions on workers.

text: Workers in your factory have complained that the loud noise of their working environment is
affecting their concentration. You decide to conduct an experiment to find out.

parts.text: Suggest how you would manage a group to reduce group conflict if you were leader.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Outline the theory on which your suggestion is based.
